devplans.shows: Sprint speed 28.2 → 27.1 → 26.3 ft/s with hamstring strains in 2026 (opened the year on the IL, returned to it in season); bat speed up to 75.4 mph (90th pct)
devplans.question: Is the speed loss a recurring hamstring problem (strength, asymmetry, sprint mechanics) rather than aging at 28?
devplans.assessment: Medical review; isometric and eccentric hamstring strength (left vs. right); force plates (CMJ asymmetry); max-velocity sprint mechanics on video
devplans.block: Eccentric hamstring program and graded sprint exposure; primary position moves to first base to cut sprint load
devplans.retest: Spring: no strength asymmetry above 10%, sprint speed 27+ ft/s; 140+ games

devplans.shows: Best contact on the team (.368 xwOBA, 16.4% barrels, 98th pct) but 93 games after a left hamstring tear in April; left shoulder surgery in 2025
devplans.question: Can his body handle an everyday workload after two straight seasons cut by injury?
devplans.assessment: Medical clearance (hamstring, shoulder); hamstring strength and asymmetry; shoulder range of motion and strength; sprint test
devplans.block: Same hamstring block as Stowers; shoulder strength maintenance; planned rest days in season
devplans.retest: Spring: cleared, no asymmetry above 10%; 550+ PA

devplans.shows: +9 OAA in center and a 22.2% chase rate (91st pct), but bat speed 70.2 mph (24th) and 3.8% barrels; left elbow discomfort, visited Dr. Keith Meister
devplans.question: Is the elbow a throwing problem that affects his defense, and can he add bat speed without losing his eye?
devplans.assessment: Imaging and medical review; throwing velocity and arm strength; bat sensor baseline
devplans.block: Return-to-throw progression; rotational power and bat-speed intent work once cleared
devplans.retest: Spring: full throwing clearance; bat speed +1 mph with the same chase rate

devplans.shows: Bat speed 64.5 → 66.9 → 68.3 mph, still 7th percentile; barrels 3.2%
devplans.question: The strength gain is real; can it continue without costing contact (13.9% K)?
devplans.assessment: Bat sensor baseline; force plates; rotational med-ball velocity

devplans.shows: Four-seam back to 97.5 mph after Tommy John (no 2024 season), but K% 17.1% (13th pct) and four-seam +6.6 runs; led MLB in innings
devplans.question: A fastball shape or location problem, not a strength one; and recovery after the heaviest workload in MLB
devplans.assessment: Four-seam movement and approach angle vs. his 2022 Cy Young season (Trackman); release consistency; recovery markers
devplans.block: Four-seam usage and location plan; lean on cutter and sinker; recovery-first offseason
devplans.retest: Spring: four-seam whiff 21%+; K% 20%+ in season

devplans.shows: 26.2% K and slider -8.2 runs, but 20 starts with neck and rib issues; .346 xwOBA the third time through
devplans.question: Trunk durability (rib, neck) and workload tolerance
devplans.assessment: Thoracic mobility; rotational and anti-rotation strength; velocity by inning and by start
devplans.block: Trunk durability block, then a throwing ramp built for 28 starts

devplans.shows: Four-seam 93.7 → 90.5 mph and sinker 93.5 → 90.4 mph in two years
devplans.question: Arm health, fatigue or mechanics?
devplans.assessment: Medical review; force plates; velocity by appearance and days of rest
devplans.retest: Spring: sinker back to 92+ mph, or a low-leverage role

devplans.shows: Four-seam 92.7 → 96.0 mph, but sinker 4.4% whiff and +8.5 runs
devplans.question: The velocity gain is physical; the problem is the sinker's shape
devplans.assessment: Sinker movement and seam orientation (Trackman, high-speed video)
devplans.block: Reduce sinker usage; lean on splitter (-6.0) and curveball (-3.2)
devplans.retest: Spring bullpens: sinker at MLB-average run value or under 15% usage

monitoring.rule: Bat speed from game data reviewed monthly; a monthly drop of 1.0+ mph triggers a strength and health check

Weekly countermovement jump on force plates in season, judged against each player's own typical error
